subject: Private gateway outbound authorization: allowlist & mTLS checklist
messages:
From: Jared Liu <jared.liu@acmehealth.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.ai>
Cc: infra-ops@acmehealth.com, laura.bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private deployment connectivity question

Michael —

Thanks for the quick sync earlier. As discussed, we're standing up a private gateway in our primary VPC and want to be clear on the minimal outbound footprint your control plane and auxiliary services require. We attach our current NAT mapping for the gateway (acme_current_nat_map.csv).

Specifically looking for:
- Exact FQDNs + ports Redwood needs to reach (control plane, artifact store, CRLs, telemetry).
- Whether you require direct outbound to public IPs or we can route through a proxy (our infra team prefers proxying everything through a corporate egress).
- mTLS or cert pinning requirements for the control-plane connection.

Our security team needs this info to produce an allowlist and firewall rule set. Please include any intermittent endpoints (OCSP, package repos) we should allow.

Jared
Head of Platform Ops
Acme Health

Attachment: acme_current_nat_map.csv (csv)
From: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.ai>
To: Jared Liu <jared.liu@acmehealth.com>
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.ai, olga.petrov@redwood.ai, neha.kapoor@redwood.ai, dev.patel@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 11:07:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment connectivity question

Hi Jared — thanks for the NAT map. Posting an initial, conservative outbound checklist below so your team can start a draft allowlist. I've also attached a CSV you can drop into your firewall tool (redwood_private_allowlist_draft.csv) and a reference diagram.

High-level guidance (minimal outbound required):
- Primary control plane: control-plane.redwood.ai (443) — TLS 1.2+; mutual TLS optional but recommended for Private deployments.
- Artifact storage / model pulls: artifacts.redwood.ai (443) — signed TLS; allow SNI for artifacts.redwood.ai.
- Telemetry/metrics: telemetry.redwood.ai (443) — we send aggregated metrics; if you proxy, allow POST to that FQDN.
- Certificate checks: ocsp.intents.redwood.ai and crl.redwood.ai (TCP 80/443) — include to avoid cert validation failures.
- Time sync & OS updates: time.acme-ntp.pool (123/UDP) and repo URLs (varies) — recommended to permit via proxy or firewall.

Ports and protocols (recommended firewall rules):
1) outbound TCP 443 to control-plane.redwood.ai, artifacts.redwood.ai, telemetry.redwood.ai (SNI allowlist recommended)
2) outbound TCP 80/443 to ocsp & crl endpoints for CRL/OCSP checks
3) outbound UDP 123 for NTP (or allow via your internal NTP relay)
4) DNS (UDP/TCP 53) to your internal resolver; if you have split-horizon, make sure private hostnames resolve to internal addresses used by the gateway

On proxying:
- Proxy is acceptable. If you route via a corporate HTTPS proxy, we need:
  * Allow CONNECT to destination FQDNs for 443
  * Preserve SNI header (some proxies rewrite SNI; that will break cert validation)
  * Allow large body sizes for artifact pulls (up to 500 MB per download) or allow direct egress for artifact endpoints

mTLS / auth:
- For Private we support either bearer token over TLS or mTLS between the gateway and our control plane. mTLS requires a client cert we will sign for you; if you choose mTLS, list the cert CN in your allowlist and allow the SNI. mTLS is strongly recommended for high-compliance customers.

IP allowlist notes:
- We publish a small set of stable egress IPs for control-plane connections; however, artifact delivery may come from geo-distributed CDN ranges. For control-plane only, allowing FQDN+port is best if your firewall supports SNI filtering. Otherwise allow the static IPs listed in our published CIDR file (see Drive link).

Operational constraints:
- Keep persistent outbound connections when possible to reduce handshake overhead; short-lived high-volume bursts (e.g., model pulls at rollout) may need temporary exceptions.
- If you use NAT pools with ephemeral IP rotation, please provide the rotation window so we can correlate connections in logs.

Next steps:
1) Laura — can you review these rules and add the internal runbook steps for our on-prem connector?
2) Jared — if you prefer mTLS, say so and we’ll begin cert provisioning.

Thanks,
Michael Grant
Sr. Product Ops, Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood_private_allowlist_draft.csv (csv); diagram-private-gateway.png (png)
From: laura.bennett@redwood.ai <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jared Liu <jared.liu@acmehealth.com>, olga.petrov@redwood.ai, neha.kapoor@redwood.ai, dev.patel@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 21 Apr 2027 08:35:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment connectivity question

Thanks Michael — I made a few operational additions and a short checklist for the firewall team. Inline edits below.

Inline: On Tue, Apr 20, 2027 at 11:07 AM Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.ai> wrote:
> High-level guidance (minimal outbound required):
> - Primary control plane: control-plane.redwood.ai (443) — TLS 1.2+; mutual TLS optional but recommended for Private deployments.

Add: For customers using strict egress appliances that only allow IP+port rules (no SNI), we recommend
- Allow list of control-plane CIDRs (published), and a small set of CDN ranges for artifacts. If CDN ranges are unacceptable, request artifact delivery via a customer-controlled ECR/S3 mirror and we will push signed packages there.

Add: SNI allowlist and Host header checks — please configure both if your firewall supports it; matching SNI is safer than IP only.

Add: CRL/OCSP — also allow outbound to our CA issuer endpoints: ca-issuer.redwood.ai (443) and the OS vendor's CRL/OCSP endpoints (we included common ones in the attached CSV).

Checklist for operations (firewall team):
- [ ] Ingest redwood_private_allowlist_draft.csv into firewall ruleset in staging namespace
- [ ] Confirm DNS resolution for control-plane.redwood.ai resolves to private IPs in split-horizon in staging
- [ ] Validate TLS handshake with and without proxy (test harness provided in Drive)
- [ ] Run artifact download test with a 250 MB payload to confirm max-body limits
- [ ] Provide NAT rotation window and sample source IPs to Redwood ops for log correlation

Security note from Olga (added):
> Please include OCSP stapling checks on your side and validate CRL refresh cadence (we recommend every 24h for high-security deployments). Also consider blocking outbound SMTP from the gateway unless explicitly needed.

Neha: confirm SOC2 requirements around logging retention for outbound connections — I noted this in the checklist items.

Laura Bennett
Principal Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

Attachment: updated-checklist.xlsx (stub referenced in Drive)
From: Jared Liu <jared.liu@acmehealth.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.ai>
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.ai, olga.petrov@redwood.ai, infra-ops@acmehealth.com
Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2027 14:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment connectivity question

Michael/Laura — thanks for the fast turnaround. We prefer to run through our corporate proxy but will enable mTLS for the control-plane connection. A few answers and one ask: 

1) NAT rotation window: 15 minutes (we'll send a sample trace).
2) We'll configure SNI pass-through and preserve Host headers on the proxy — confirmed with infra.
3) We agree to allow outbound UDP 123 to our internal NTP relay only (we will not permit public NTP directly).
4) Regarding OCSP/CRL: our appliance blocks unknown external cert-check endpoints; we will allow the CA issuer (ca-issuer.redwood.ai) and ocsp.intents.redwood.ai.

Attached is our updated allowlist export (acme_allowlist_final.csv) which maps the NAT translations and proxy egress IP set. Please confirm the mTLS client cert CN format you need and the provisioning timeline.

Brief note for Redwood ops: if needed for debugging, our infra@acmehealth.com can open a 1-hour support window with the firewall team during your test timeframe.

Jared
Head of Platform Ops, Acme Health

Attachment: acme_allowlist_final.csv (csv)
